scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The fouetté en tournant was introduced in the Grand Pas d'azione of the ballet Cinderella on December 17, 1893, with choreography by Lev Ivanov, Enrico Cecchetti, and Marius Petipa, and music by Baron Boris Vietinghoff-Scheel.
Pierina Legnani performed 32 consecutive fouettés without traveling, a feat reported by St. Petersburg Gazette critic Konstantin Skalkovski.
Legnani repeated this in Swan Lake (1895), and Mathilde Kschesinskaya later achieved the same milestone.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Performing 32 consecutive fouettés is considered a bravura demonstration of a ballerina's strength, stamina, and technique.
It is a highly difficult feat that many dancers can execute on only one side, usually the right.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: A fouetté turn begins standing on one flat foot in plié with the knee bent.
The working leg is extended and whipped to the side to create momentum, then pulled into a retiré or passé position while the supporting foot rises to relevé or en pointe.
This creates the angular momentum needed for a rotation in place.
Watch for 32 consecutive fouettés.

Formation: rotating in place on the supporting foot without traveling

scenes.title: Step A — slowly
